answer: In vision, the dimensionality label describes what a system recovers from images: 2D perception works in the image plane (low-level cues like depth maps, optical flow, segmentation and camera parameters), 3D perception/reconstruction lifts those cues into spatial geometry of a static scene (point clouds, meshes, neural fields or Gaussian splats), and 4D adds time, recovering a temporally consistent 3D representation of a moving, deforming scene. A useful mental model is a hierarchy: 2D cues feed 3D reconstruction, and 4D methods extend 3D either by learning a canonical shape plus a deformation field over time or by making the representation itself time-dependent. Typical tasks per level are depth/flow estimation (2D), multi-view stereo, SfM/SLAM and 3D Gaussian splatting (3D), and dynamic novel-view synthesis, non-rigid tracking and motion capture (4D).

citations.title: General 4D Dynamic Scene Reconstruction from Multiple View Video (thesis)
